method.head: 7eb59008f7d8e156e81fd18a57658fdef2553264
checks: Full 50 MiB source consumed; valid JSON; source reader released
Exact surviving property counts, name lengths and last-winner values
Independent streamed expected output byte length and SHA-256; <=64 KiB output pages
method.shapes: 16 long keys, unique ASCII / UTF-8 replacement, repeated identical ASCII key, or 12 overwritten replacement-key subtree entries + 4 surviving entries. Trailing whitespace fills exact 50 MiB.
method.natural: Discrete process memory samples at source reads, large joins, own key definitions, parse completion, explicit post-parse GC, downstream pulls and final GC. No GC injection in restoration.
method.gcProbe: Separate diagnostic processes force GC before/after large native joins and key definitions. This shows eligible retention, NOT natural peaks, runtime capacity or normal throughput.
method.metrics: heapUsed+external is computed at the same instant; arrayBuffers is a subset of external. observedMaximum is max of samples, not a continuous allocation peak. Baseline subtraction is per child.
limitations: Natural replacement-key observed maximum increased in this single comparison; not hidden or claimed as a uniform memory improvement.
Native property keys remain complete strings. Full result holding barely changes; natural GC scheduling can defer collection of eligible token pages.
Unlike the previous usage harness, this final releasedAfterGc stage does not deliberately hold a complete output/audit string.
GC-probe hooks do extra forced collection; compare like-labelled runs only.
